text: The last working gantries will go on charging until the 31st of December 2026; from the 1st of January 2027 the charge arrives by satellite instead, and the sign that a charged road lies ahead will be an oval of blue paint on the tarmac.

It is the end of the most visible piece of a system that does something no other country attempts in quite the same way: it makes a driver pay for permission to own a car, and then pay again, per trip, to drive it.

On the 2nd of June 1975 the Area Licensing Scheme (ALS) began: to drive into a Restricted Zone of about 6.7 square kilometres around the city centre during the morning peak, a motorist bought a paper licence — 3 Singapore dollars a day, or 60 Singapore dollars a month — and displayed it on the windscreen.

The first bidding exercise was held on the 2nd of April 1990, and from the 1st of May that year nobody could register a car in Singapore without first winning the right to: a Certificate of Entitlement, the COE.

It was cut to 1.5 per cent in 2009, 1 per cent in 2012, 0.5 per cent in 2013, 0.25 per cent in 2015, and from February 2018 it has been zero for cars and motorcycles: the fleet is not permitted to grow at all.
On the 18th of October 2023, Category B set an all-time record of 150,001 Singapore dollars and the open category 158,004 Singapore dollars — the certificate alone costing more than most cars.
Traffic responded as it had in 1975: expressway volumes fell by about 15 per cent, and average speeds in the charged hours rose from 35 to 55 kilometres an hour.
The two systems are designed as a pair, and the LTA says so in as many words: the Vehicle Quota System "regulates vehicle ownership, while ERP manages usage".
The result is the most expensive place in the world to buy a car, by a wide margin.

Then she did the sums on the daily drive — the long run in to work, down the Central Expressway and under its gantries, twice a day — and found it cheaper to rent a place of her own, chosen so that no long daily drive is needed.

On the 1st of January 2027, charging by satellite begins at the same locations, at rates under the same framework — the first adjustment of the new era is a 1 Singapore dollars rise at two locations on the Central and Pan-Island Expressways from the 4th of January.
